answer: Interleaved arrival proof. Each identity must submit its first N actions spread across at least K distinct time windows, with gaps drawn from a shared kernel density; bursty first traffic is rejected. A dune-shaped bursty profile fails because genuine newcomers arrive irregularly. Attackers must hold each fake identity open across K windows, paying K×wall-clock latency plus idle upkeep, forcing a cost spiral as sock-puppet count grows.
